rationale: The workflow already includes dependency caching (coursier/cache-action@v9) and an explicit job timeout (timeout-minutes: 30), so the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE and P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT/P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT timeout additions are already addressed. The matrix tests two Java versions (17 and 25); enabling P-LIT-FAIL-FAST risks cancelling a required matrix outcome, which conflicts with the pattern contraindication that every matrix outcome may be required, and required_checks are not verified. Reducing the 30-minute timeout is not supported by sufficient history: the CI history shows only five short runs (~1-2.5 minutes), and SBT cold builds on Java 17/Java 25 could exceed a tighter bound, violating the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT contraindication that valid slow runs must not exceed the limit. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is simulation-estimate evidence and would require a concurrency group; given the schedule trigger and unverified required-check status, cancelling in-progress runs could affect required checks. No other pattern (Bazel, test selection, build selection, environment reuse) applies to this SBT/Java workflow. Preserving intended build and test coverage means no change is warranted.
